title: WPMS/343/2010 of DR RAJENDRA SINGH Vs MAKHAN SINGH

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Writ Petition No. 343 (M/S) of 2010
 Dr. Rajendra Singh S/o late Sri Prem Bahadur -Petitioner
 Versus
 Makhan Singh S/o Sri Kheel Singh - Respondent
 Sri Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the petitioner
 Sri J.P. Joshi, Senior Advocate along with Sri Dinesh Gahatori
 Advocate for the respondent.
Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J. (Oral).
Heard Sri Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the petitioner and Sri J.P.
Joshi, Senior Advocate, along with Sri Dinesh Gahatori, Advocate for
the respondent.
 By means of this petition the petitioner has sought a writ in the
nature of certiorari for quashing the order dated 10-2-2010 passed by
Addl. District Judge Rishikesh in Misc. Civil Appeal No. 156/2006
Dr. Rajendra Singh vs. Makhan Singh whereby the appeal was
dismissed as well as the order dated 31-8-2006 passed by Civil Judge
(J.D.) Rishikesh in O.S. No. 297/2005, whereby the application of the
petitioner for temporary injunction was dismissed and the temporary
injunction application of the respondent filed along with counter claim
was allowed and the petitioner-plaintiff was directed not to interfere
with the possession of the defendant- respondent on plot No.9 area
225 square yards which has been purchased by way of sale deed from
Avnish Kumar Goyal.
 The appellant-petitioner preferred appeal under Order 43 Rule
1(r) against the order passed by trial court which was dismissed.
Hence this petition.
 During the course of argument, the learned counsel for the
petitioner has contended and limited his argument only to plot No.10
that the trial court as well as the appellate court have also held that the
plaintiff-petitioner is the owner of plot No.10 and the defendant-respondent has also given undertaking in para-29 of his W.S. to the
effect that if injunction is granted in favour of plaintiff regarding plot
No.10, area 125.25 square meters, which has been purchased by way
of sale deed dated 5-7-1991 will not interfere in his possession.

2
 In view of the admission made in para-29 of W.S. as well as on
the basis of finding of both the courts below prima facie it is evident
that petitioner-plaintiff is owner in possession of plot No.10 only and
he is entitled to get temporary injunction in his favour in respect of
plot No.10.
 The writ petition is partly allowed. The temporary injunction
application 6-C/2 moved by petitioner-plaintiff in the suit is partly
allowed only to the extent that the defendant-respondent shall not
interfere in the peaceful possession of plaintiff-petitioner of plot
No.10 area 125.25 square meters, which has been purchased by the
petitioner by way of sale deed dated 5-7-1991 and in view of
undertaking given by defendant in para-29 of his W.S. The impugned
orders are accordingly modified. Order passed on temporary
injunction application of defendant, whereby the petitioner was
directed not to interfere in peaceful possession of defendant in respect
of plot No. 9, referred above, is maintained.
ISB (B.S. Verma, J.)
 02-09-2013
